thread:
Anna: AcmeCorp reported auth failures from their Dedicated private deployment. Symptoms: some requests succeed, many get 401 from our API gateway. They say the client sends a signed cookie and our LB should rewrite it into Authorization: Bearer <token>. Intermittent — ~30% requests missing auth header after a period of time.

AcmeCorp-SRE: Repro steps we used:
1) curl -v to NLB IP with cookie header:
   curl -v -H 'Cookie: SSO_SIG=v1|eyJhb...' https://acme.example.com/v1/chat 
   -> first request returns 200. Next ~3 requests return 401. No client-side change.

AcmeCorp-SRE: We added extra logging in their ingress lua (edge) that does cookie->Authorization rewrite. Logs show rewrite executed, but backend (our envoy) doesn't always receive Authorization. Packet counts look normal.

Anna: Thanks. Which infra? NLB -> F5 -> Istio (Envoy) inside VPC (Dedicated pool). They said sessionAffinity by cookie is enabled on F5.

Raj: Oof. F5 is a wildcard here. Quick checks: header truncation vs header drop vs connection reuse. Can you paste the edge lua log showing rewrite + subsequent request?

AcmeCorp-SRE: Pasted snippet:
```
[edge-lua] rewrite cookie->auth: ok token_len=342 ts=2025-11-02T10:12:11Z
[edge-lua] proxy to f5: keepalive conn=10
[edge-lua] rewrite cookie->auth: ok token_len=342 ts=2025-11-02T10:12:15Z
[edge-lua] proxy to f5: keepalive conn=9
```
Backend (envoy) access logs: only first request has `Authorization` entry. next requests from same client IP do not.

Mei: Could be connection pooling + F5 iRule dropping Authorization on connection reuse. I've seen devices that strip auth on reused TCP conn for security/iRule reasons. Ask them for tcpdump at the F5 VIP to see headers on the wire.

Lucas: Also check for HTTP/1.1 pipelining or chunked transfer oddities. But given keepalive conn decrement, looks like reuse. Can we see F5 logs?

AcmeCorp-SRE: We captured tcpdump on edge host (pre-F5). It shows Authorization present in packets sent to F5. But on packets leaving F5 to our Envoy, Authorization header missing for subsequent requests on same TCP flow.

Raj: That nails it -> F5 is removing header mid-connection. Two possibilities: iRule that strips Authorization based on cookie length or SSO cookie marker, or a rewrite/SSL offload quirk when request considered 'subsequent'. Ask F5 team to dump iRules for VIP.

AcmeCorp-SRE: F5 iRule excerpt: (they redacted ips)
```
when HTTP_REQUEST {
  if { [HTTP::header exists "Authorization"] } {
    if { [HTTP::header length "Authorization"] > 300 } {
      # drop header for 'long tokens'
      HTTP::header remove "Authorization"
      log local0. "long auth stripped"
    }
  }
}
```

Anna: Wow. That is the behavior. The first request somehow sends token <= 300? But logs show 342 len. Strange.

Mei: Maybe the rewrite writes cookie->auth, then some intermediate normalization compresses token (base64 padding?) and first packet ended up split so length calculation different. But the rule clearly removes headers >300. That would explain intermittent. Tokens sometimes shortened by compressing claims (maybe compression or a signed cookie variant).

Lucas: Short-term mitigations: 1) Have F5 remove that iRule or bump threshold; 2) Change edge lua to emit a short-lived opaque token (hash) that maps server-side to the long token (so Authorization header length < 300); 3) Force connection close so each request is new TCP flow (stop keepalive) — not great for perf.

AcmeCorp-SRE: We temporarily disabled keepalive on edge proxy and errors stopped. So keepalive + iRule condition is the trigger.

Raj: Root cause summary: F5 iRule removes long Authorization headers on reused connections. First request can bypass depending on how lengths computed; subsequent requests are stripped.

Mei: Runtime suggestion if they can't touch F5 immediately — add a short middleware that exchanges long signed cookie for a short opaque token and set `Authorization: Bearer <short>` before sending to F5. Provide example Lua snippet: 
```
-- pseudo: sign->opaque map
local long = request:get_cookie('SSO_SIG')
local short = hash(long):sub(1,32)
-- store mapping in redis/kvs and set header
request:set_header('Authorization','Bearer '..short)
```

Anna: Customer applied short-token exchange and rollbacked iRule later. They also committed to removing the length-based strip in F5.

AcmeCorp-SRE: Confirmed resolution: after iRule tweak (remove strip) and optional short-token middleware, 0 auth failures in 6h. Thanks team! :tada:

deploy-bot: Deployment 2025-11-02T11:00Z for acme-edge succeeded (short-token middleware toggled on).

Anna: Marking support case resolved. Will follow up with postmortem steps for customers using legacy iRules.

Raj: +1. Suggest we add a note in docs: "Edge devices may strip Authorization on connection reuse; avoid header-length-based iRules or use token exchange."

Mei: I'll add an internal runbook entry with tcpdump signs and mitigation checklist.

Anna: Closing thread.
